requirement_text: Certificate of general university entry qualification (Abitur): eligible for all courses of study. A vocational university entry qualification (fachgebundene Hochschulreife) is limited to specified programmes. Applicants may also qualify via successfully completed undergraduate studies, or via the Delta-Prüfung (an examination that can extend a subject-restricted entrance qualification to additional subjects).

requirement_text: International applicants should consult the DAAD database, which 'provides an initial indication of whether your previous educational qualifications entitle you to study in Germany', and the anabin database maintained by the Central Office for Foreign Education (ZAB). Applicants from 'convention countries' (EU member states plus a list including Switzerland, Turkey and Norway) are evaluated using anabin guidelines through the C@MPUS portal. For other countries, a secondary school leaving certificate that qualifies the holder for higher-education studies in their home country is required, evaluated for equivalency to the German Abitur standard.

requirement_text: International prospective students whose foreign diploma does not qualify them for admission to a German university may be referred to a Preparatory College (Studienkolleg). The prerequisite for the preparatory college is having at least 500 to 800 hours of German language learning. The course runs two semesters and prepares students for the assessment test ('Feststellungsprüfung'), which must be completed in no more than four semesters (including the starting semester).

researcher_notes: Notable: Universität Stuttgart does not operate its own Studienkolleg. Applicants pursuing technical degrees are referred to the Studienkolleg at Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT); applicants for humanities, linguistics or economics programmes are referred to Ruprecht-Karls-Universität Heidelberg's Studienkolleg. No exemptions from this pathway were stated on the fetched page for applicants whose diplomas fall short.

researcher_notes: Statutory requirement under Baden-Württemberg state law (LHG), not Stuttgart-specific, but Stuttgart enforces it at enrollment. requirement_text: The University of Stuttgart requires proof of German language proficiency from all study applicants. Accepted certifications: TestDaF level 4 or better in all four parts of the test (TestDaF 4x4); Goethe-Zertifikat C1 or C2; the German Language Diploma (Deutsches Sprachdiplom, DSD) Level II from the Standing Conference of the Ministers of Education and Cultural Affairs; telc Deutsch C1 Hochschule; the German language examination for university admission for foreign applicants (DSH) with an overall result of DSH-2 or above; the Austrian Language Diploma C2 (ÖSD C2); the German Language Test II from the Munich Language and Interpreting Institute; or a degree whose courses were instructed in the German language.

researcher_notes: uni-assist finding (this research wave's specific question): Universität Stuttgart does NOT use uni-assist.de for any applicant population. This page, fetched directly, names C@MPUS as the sole application system for all three listed applicant groups, with no mention of uni-assist anywhere on this page or the parallel /en/study/application/ overview page.
